execution: Generated Python stays in Monty. Approved numerical calls execute in a separate CPython SciPy worker. No arbitrary Python callbacks, code strings, SQL, files or network APIs are exposed.
numeric_policy: Scientific operations convert numeric inputs to float64, except integer sampling indices/counts. Keep original SQL Decimal values for accounting totals and monetary cluster averages; use returned labels/indices to calculate these exactly in Monty. Results include method, RNG and library-version metadata.
randomness: Each call uses an independent Generator(PCG64) initialized from SeedSequence([seed, stream]). Use different stream values for independent batches; retrying the same seed/stream repeats draws. NumPy draws differ from Python random even with the same seed.

kmeans.signature: kmeans(observations: list[list[Number]], *, clusters: int = 3, max_iterations: int = 50, standardize: bool = True, initialization: str = 'farthest_first', seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
kmeans.description: SciPy kmeans2 on a finite rectangular matrix. Returns labels in input order, centroids, counts, convergence and method metadata. Standardization uses population standard deviation and ignores constant dimensions. Farthest-first initialization starts with the first input row; sort observations by the required entity ID first. Fewer distinct profiles produce fewer clusters. Monetary averages should be recomputed from original Decimal rows using labels.

bootstrap.signature: bootstrap(values: list[Number], *, statistic: str = 'mean', n_resamples: int = 1000, confidence_level: float = 0.95, method: str = 'percentile', quantile_method: str = 'nearest_rank', seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
bootstrap.description: SciPy bootstrap for mean, median, sum or population std. Returns estimate, lower/upper confidence bounds, standard error, bootstrap distribution and method metadata. Nearest-rank bounds use inverted-CDF quantiles and require percentile method; basic/BCa require quantile_method='linear'. Inspect warnings and degeneracy.

sample.signature: sample(distribution: str, parameters: dict[str, Any], *, size: int | list[int] = 1000, seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
sample.description: Generate batched SciPy random draws for general Monte Carlo calculations inside Monty. Distributions: normal/uniform use loc and positive scale; binomial uses integer n and probability p; bernoulli uses p. Vector parameters can broadcast against size, e.g. probabilities per cohort and size=[1000, cohort_count]. Returns samples, shape and method metadata. Aggregate domain-specific outcomes in Monty, preserving Decimal money.

binomial.signature: binomial(n: int, p: float, *, size: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
binomial.description: SciPy binomial draws plus theoretical mean/variance. n is a nonnegative trial count and p is in [0,1]. For vector probabilities use sample.

bernoulli.signature: bernoulli(p: float = 0.5, *, size: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
bernoulli.description: SciPy coin flips (0/1) with probability p, plus theoretical mean/variance.

resample_indices.signature: resample_indices(n_observations: int, *, n_resamples: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
resample_indices.description: NumPy sampling with replacement: returns an n_resamples by n_observations index matrix. Use indices to implement custom statistics on original Decimal rows in Monty without passing sandbox functions into CPython.

monte_carlo_test.signature: monte_carlo_test(values: list[Number], *, distribution: str = 'normal', parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, statistic: str = 'mean', n_resamples: int = 1000, alternative: str = 'two-sided', seed: int = 42, stream: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
monte_carlo_test.description: SciPy Monte Carlo hypothesis test for a named distribution and statistic (mean, median, sum, std). Returns observed statistic, p-value, null distribution and method metadata. This is a hypothesis test, not a general portfolio-loss forecast; use sample for simulation of outcomes.

calling_convention: All functions are async host operations: import scientific; result = await scientific.kmeans(matrix). Monty supports top-level await. Await results before indexing; do not return coroutine objects.
